context_summary: User tested the F07 frontend dashboard and found three issues: (1) card names are double-encoded (UTF-8 bytes stored as latin-1, e.g. 'Contramagica' shows as garbled text), (2) market movers show 0% change because frontend defaults to period=7d but MYP price observations are weekly, (3) only 30 cards from 1 set (DMR) — insufficient data for meaningful market intelligence. Database has 30 cards, 1889 observations spanning 2023-08-20 to 2026-08-16.

options_considered.description: Single feature F08 covering encoding fix + movers period default fix + collection expansion to more sets.
pros: All three issues are facets of the same user complaint: 'the dashboard shows garbage' — fixing them together delivers a coherent improvement
The encoding fix and movers period fix are small (< 1 hour each) and would feel under-scoped as standalone features
Collection expansion validates the encoding fix end-to-end with fresh data
Single PRD, single set of diagrams, single QA pass — lower overhead
User gets a fully working dashboard in one delivery instead of needing 2-3 feature cycles
cons: Mixing data-quality bugfixes with a feature (expansion) in one feature number
Collection expansion involves network I/O to MYP — potential for flakiness in CI
Larger blast radius if something goes wrong

options_considered.description: Split into F08 (encoding fix + movers period fix — data quality) and F09 (collection expansion to more sets).
pros: Clean separation of concerns: bugfix vs. new capability
F08 ships fast (no network I/O, no scraping), F09 can be planned separately
If collection expansion hits Cloudflare issues, encoding fix is already shipped
cons: Two feature cycles for what the user perceives as one problem ('dashboard is broken')
The encoding fix alone still leaves the dashboard with only 30 DMR cards showing flat prices — user value is low
Double the overhead: 2 PRDs, 2 Architect plans, 2 QA passes, 2 commits
F08 without expansion would fix names but the dashboard would still feel empty and useless

options_considered.description: Fix encoding + movers period as a quick bugfix (no feature number), defer collection expansion entirely.
pros: Fastest path to fixing the most visible bugs
cons: Skips the project's established feature workflow — sets a bad precedent
Dashboard remains nearly useless with only 30 cards from 1 set
Movers will still show minimal change because DMR prices genuinely don't move much — the real fix needs more diverse data
The user explicitly mentioned expanding to more sets as part of the scope

rationale: Option A is the right call for three reasons. First, the three issues are deeply interdependent: fixing encoding alone still shows a broken dashboard (30 flat-price cards), and expanding collection without fixing encoding would just produce more garbled names. They must ship together for the user to see a working product. Second, the encoding fix and movers period default are both small, surgical changes (parser encoding + frontend default state) that would be under-scoped as standalone features — bundling them with collection expansion creates a properly-sized feature. Third, collection expansion naturally validates the encoding fix with fresh data from new sets, making it a superior integration test compared to only re-processing existing DMR data. The risk of a larger blast radius is mitigated by the wave structure: Wave 0 fixes encoding + movers (low risk, no I/O), Wave 1 handles collection expansion (isolated, can be tested independently). If expansion hits issues, the bugfixes are already committed.

scope.title: Data enrichment & encoding fix
deliverables: Fix UTF-8 double-encoding in parser (likely curl_cffi response decoding) and migrate existing DB data
Change frontend movers default period from 7d to 30d for meaningful price changes
Expand collection beyond DMR — add at least 3-5 popular sets with significant price movement
Validate end-to-end: dashboard shows correct names, meaningful movers, and richer card catalog
out_of_scope: Card images from Scryfall (defer to F09+)
New API endpoints — existing endpoints are sufficient

wave_sketch.wave_0: Encoding fix (parser + DB migration script) + movers period default fix (frontend)
wave_sketch.wave_1: Collection expansion infrastructure — parameterize backfill for multiple sets, select target sets
wave_sketch.wave_2: Run expanded backfill, validate data, update docs/diagrams

governance: Gandalf T-800 strategic decision — single feature covering all three issues for maximum user value per delivery cycle
